co_3_astronomy_wall.blurb: Astronomy Wall is a small wall at the far right end of the Pooka buttress, in the Staunton Rocks section of Staunton State Park southwest of Denver, sitting near 8,800 feet. Eleven routes share the face: mostly bolted sport lines, plus a pair of trad climbs and one top-rope. Grades start at an easy 5.5 and top out around 5.11, but most of the lines cluster in the 5.10 range, which makes it a good stop for someone stepping up into double digits. The face catches sun early and slides into shade by late afternoon. A dark water streak marks the most visible line, and the route names follow a space theme.

co_abbey_the.blurb: The Abbey is a peaceful, out-of-the-way group of rocks in the South Platte region, around 8,100 feet, within the Goose Creek granite-dome country. Slabs of modest angle define it, and the lines went in with bolts placed from the ground up. Eleven routes are on record: nine sport and two trad, with some top-rope options and a few boulder problems too. Most of the climbing is easy to moderate, running from 5.3 up through the 5.9 range, with a handful of harder ones topping out at a single 5.12 project. It is a good pick for newer leaders and anyone who wants solitude over a big roster of lines.

co_hidden_falls.blurb: Hidden Falls is a winter ice and mixed venue in the Wild Basin corner of Rocky Mountain National Park, near Estes Park, at roughly 9,000 feet. The main flow is a single short pitch of around 75 to 90 feet, with side flows and mixed lines beside it. Of the eleven climbs here, ten are ice, running from WI1 up to WI6 with a good share at WI4 and WI5, plus one mixed line. Trees above the falls serve for top-rope setups. It is among the more popular ice outings in the park thanks to a short approach, so expect company, and the trees hide the falls until you are close.

co_cube_area_the.blurb: The Cube Area is a bouldering spot within the Dark Side hillside, a shady boulder field near Morrison on the Front Range. The centerpiece is a big, freestanding cube-shaped block about halfway up the main trail, with eleven problems spread over its sides, back and front. Grades run from V1 to V5, and most sit around V3, so it suits climbers who have moved past the beginner grades. The hillside is known for cooler, shaded lines in summer. The trail uphill has stone steps and passes a smaller warm-up traverse wall just above the cube. Rattlesnakes are known to be around.

co_little_dude.blurb: Little Dude is a short southwest-facing crag in Golden Gate Canyon State Park near Golden, close to Dude's Fishing Hole and a short walk from Dude's Throne. Routes run only about 25 to 60 feet, so it works well as a half-day stop or an add-on to a day at the neighboring cliff. Eleven climbs, mostly bolted sport with a couple of trad lines, are on offer. The grades skew hard: three around 5.9, then a cluster of 5.12s plus single 5.11 and 5.13 lines. The crag is tucked away and hard to pick out on a first visit.
